stemKinds.description: The infinitive minus -en (lernen → lern) or minus -n for -eln/-ern verbs (lächeln → lächel). Default.
The whole infinitive (used by the wir/Sie imperative: "lernen wir", "lernen Sie", and by Futur I / Konjunktiv II after werden/würde).
An ending containing % is a template around the stem: Partizip II "ge%t" → ge+lern+t. Spelling rules may strip the ge- (prefix verbs, -ieren).

A verb in "separable" is split into prefix + base (anfangen → an + fangen). Finite forms conjugate the base and append the prefix ("fange an"); Partizip II is prefix + base participle ("angefangen"); compound tenses use the whole infinitive ("werde anfangen").

perfekt.note: sein for verbs of movement / change of state (list); a separable verb inherits its base verb unless listed itself

konjunktiv2.note: würde + infinitive for regular verbs; sein/haben/werden, the modals, wissen and common strong verbs carry their own forms in irregulars

spelling.when: stem ends in -t/-d, or in -m/-n after a consonant other than l/r/m/n/h (arbeiten → arbeitest, arbeitete; atmen, rechnen): an e is inserted before -st/-t/-te
same stems: Partizip II ends in -et (gearbeitet)
-ieren and -igen verbs keep the -e in the du-imperative (studiere!, entschuldige!)
stem ends in s/ß/z/x: du-form takes -t instead of -st (heißen → du heißt, tanzen → du tanzt)
-eln verbs drop the e of the stem in the ich-form (lächeln → ich lächle)
inseparable prefix (be-, emp-, ent-, er-, ge-, miss-, ver-, zer-, über-, unter-, um-, durch-, wieder-, hinter-, wider-) or -ieren: Partizip II has no ge- (besucht, studiert)
